ai.summary: The U.S. is moving to require licenses for some overseas data centers that provide substantial computing power to firms in high-risk countries, including China. The rule is intended to curb remote access to advanced U.S. AI chips and close a route around existing export restrictions.
ai.title: US tightens chip controls on data centers supplying remote access

ai.summary: California sued OpenAI, alleging inadequate safeguards and monitoring contributed to a July 2026 cyberattack involving Hugging Face. The complaint seeks remedies under public-nuisance and unfair-competition law; its allegations have not been adjudicated.
ai.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks

ai.summary: A Reuters review of more than 300 documents found that Chinese researchers and companies are increasingly using outputs from leading U.S. AI models to train domestic alternatives through distillation. The practice may help China build capable, lower-cost systems while facing tighter access to advanced chips.
ai.title: Exclusive-China taps US AI models to train homegrown rivals as chip curbs bite

ai.summary: AMD said it had completed its acquisition of AI research startup World Labs and that founder Fei-Fei Li would join as executive vice president and chief scientist. World Labs develops world models for interactive 3D environments and robotic learning.
ai.title: AMD completes World Labs deal, names Fei-Fei Li chief scientist

ai.summary: Washington’s latest restrictions on access to advanced AI chips helped put pressure on technology stocks as U.S.-China technology tensions intensified. Reuters reported that investors were also watching Nvidia’s upcoming results and the company’s leadership turmoil.
ai.title: Markets shaken, not stirred, as US-China tech war heats up

quantum.summary: IBM, NVIDIA and Fermilab announced plans for a quantum-classical codesign platform, bringing NVIDIA GPU systems together with IBM quantum computers. Researchers will use it to study error correction, hybrid applications and modular architectures linking multiple quantum processors.
quantum.title: IBM, Fermilab, and NVIDIA Announce Plans for New Co-Design Platform to Accelerate the Development of Next-Generation, Modular Quantum Computers

quantum.summary: NVIDIA's TCBP-JOBS preprint reports up to 13,000 times faster decoding than unsparsified long-beam Tesseract on selected bivariate-bicycle-code benchmarks. Results depend on code, noise level and comparator settings; this is a classical decoding benchmark, not a general quantum-computing speedup.
quantum.title: NVIDIA reports GPU decoding speedups on selected error-correction benchmarks

quantum.summary: Researchers report up to an 18-fold reduction in logical infidelity in simulations of qubit codes under modeled drifting noise, compared with the same learned code without adaptive retuning. The strongest result required slow drift and high sampling rates; it was not demonstrated on physical hardware. This November 17 article covers a preprint first posted September 4, 2025 and revised July 14, 2026.
quantum.title: Adaptive Error Correction Improves Simulated Qubit Performance

quantum.summary: A theoretical and numerical study designs closed-loop control pulses to suppress unwanted coupling during single-qubit gates in modeled two- and three-qubit systems. The November 17 coverage discusses a preprint first posted in March 2025 and revised in June 2026, not a new hardware demonstration.
quantum.title: Numerical study uses geometric pulse design to improve modeled qubit gates

quantum.summary: BlueQubit selected eight research teams for grants supporting work on quantum advantage, error correction and classical simulation of quantum-computing claims. The program offers awards of $10,000–$40,000 in computing and AI credits, with support from IBM, AWS and NVIDIA.
quantum.title: BlueQubit Selects Eight Teams for Quantum Flywheel Grant Programme

quantum.summary: Moth says its Tessa method encoded 1,568 numbers across all 120 qubits of an IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processor and recovered the encoded image. The company described this as a data-encoding record; the report notes the hardware’s output remains imperfect.
quantum.title: A Breakthrough That Really Counts - New Record for Encoding and Reading Back Data on a Quantum Computer
